status.en: 243 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Kyiv, Moscow and Odesa.
status.nb: 243 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Kyiv, Moscow og Odesa.

summary.en: Recent days show a sharp escalation of both diplomatic and military pressures: a disputed diesel deal has sparked calls for a new Ukrainian president, while Ukraine is intensifying precision drone strikes on Russian oil refineries and targeting Russian tech sites such as Yandex data centres. Russia continues to use glide‑bomb attacks, killing dozens in Zaporizhzhia, and conducts drone strikes on civilian infrastructure, including a deadly attack in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast. These developments add a political dimension to the ongoing violence, linking high‑level negotiations with intensified targeting of energy and technology assets. The conflict has already caused 75,767 battle‑related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: De siste dagene har både diplomatiske og militære spenninger skutt i været: en omstridt dieselforhandling har ført til krav om en ny ukrainsk president, mens Ukraina intensiverer presisjons‑dronangrep mot russiske oljeraffinerier og rammer russisk teknologiinfrastruktur som Yandex‑datasentre. Russland fortsetter med glide‑bombeangrep som har drept flere i Zaporizjzja, og utfører dronstrike mot sivil infrastruktur, inkludert et dødelig angrep i Dnipropetrovsk oblast. Disse utviklingene gir konflikten en politisk dimensjon ved å knytte høytstående forhandlinger til økt målretting av energi‑ og teknologiatferd. Konflikten har allerede forårsaket 75 767 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)
background.extract: On 24 February 2022, Russia invaded Ukraine, starting the largest and deadliest war in Europe since World War II, in a major escalation of the existing war between the two countries that began when Russia attacked Ukraine in 2014. The fighting has caused hundreds of thousands of military casualties and tens of thousands of Ukrainian civilian casualties. Russian troops occupy roughly 20% of Ukraine. From a population of 41 million, about 8 million Ukrainians have been internally displaced and 6–7 million have fled the country, creating Europe's largest refugee crisis since World War II.
